title: Sismo de 7.8 grados con epicentro en Colima y afectaciones en Michoacán, Colima y Jalisco.
text: El terremoto de Colima de 2003 fue un sismo ocurrido a las 20:06:34 hora local del 21 de enero de 2003, frente a las costas del estado de Colima, en el oeste de México. El terremoto alcanzó una magnitud de 7,6 (MW), aunque otras instituciones estimaron diversas magnitudes que van desde 7.7,​ 7.8, y 8.0 (MW).​ Todo el estado y algunas zonas de Michoacán y Jalisco fueron afectadas por el sismo.

title: Se publicó en el Diario Oficial de la Federación la Ley General de Derechos Lingüísticos para los Pueblos Indígenas con la cual se creó el Instituto Nacional de Lenguas Indígenas.
text: El Instituto Nacional de Lenguas Indígenas (en maya yucateco: Noj Mola'ayil Máasewal T'aano'ob)​ es un organismo mexicano descentralizado perteneciente a la Administración Pública Federal,​ con personalidad jurídica y patrimonio propios, sectorizado, al momento de su creación, en la Secretaría de Educación Pública, establecido en el capítulo IV de su ley de creación: la Ley General de Derechos Lingüísticos de los …

title: Monterrey se coronó campeón del Torneo Clausura de fútbol.
text: El Torneo Clausura 2003 fue la edición LXIX del campeonato de liga de la Primera División del fútbol mexicano; Se trató del 14º torneo corto, luego del cambio en el formato de competencia, con el que se cerró la temporada 2002-03. Monterrey ganó el campeonato por segunda vez luego de 17 años sin ser campeón al Morelia.

title: Se generó la tormenta tropical Bill.
text: La tormenta tropical Bill fue una tormenta tropical que afectó la costa del golfo de Estados Unidos en el verano de 2003. La segunda tormenta de la temporada de huracanes del Atlántico de 2003, Bill se desarrolló a partir de una onda tropical el 29 de junio al norte de la península de Yucatán.

title: Se efectuaron Elecciones en el Distrito Federal para elegir 16 jefes delegacionales y 66 diputados locales.
text: Las Elecciones del Distrito Federal de 2003 se llevaron a cabo el domingo 6 de julio de 2003, simultáneamente con las elecciones federales, y en ellas fueron renovados los titulares de los siguientes cargos de elección popular del Distrito Federal: 16 Jefes Delegacionales. Titulares de cada una de las Delegaciones Políticas, equivalentes a los Municipios en el Distrito Federal.
wiki: Elecciones locales del Distrito Federal de México de 2003

title: Se efectuaron Elecciones Federales para elegir 500 diputados.
text: Las elecciones federales de México de 2003 se celebraron el domingo 6 de julio de ese año, y en ellas se votaron y se renovaron, a nivel federal, los cargos​ de 500 Diputados Federales, miembros de la cámara baja del Congreso de la Unión, 300 de ellos elegidos por el principio de mayoría relativa en distritos uninominales y 200 elegidos por el principio de representación proporcional en 5 circunscripciones plurino…

title: La selección nacional de fútbol americano perdió la final contra Japón en la Copa Mundial de Fútbol Americano.
text: La Copa Mundial de Fútbol americano de 2003 fue el segundo campeonato mundial de fútbol americano disputado en Alemania. Los estadios sede fueron el Herbert Dröse Stadion y el Berliner Strasse Stadion.
wiki: Copa Mundial de Fútbol Americano de 2003

title: La selección nacional de fútbol se coronó campeón de la Copa Oro venciendo a Brasil, un gol a cero.
text: La Copa de Oro de la Concacaf 2003 fue la decimoséptima edición del torneo continental de selecciones organizado por la Concacaf, que se realizó en los Estados Unidos y México en el mes de julio, siendo México coanfitrión por segunda vez después de 10 años. Al igual que en la edición anterior participaron 12 selecciones nacionales, con dos invitados provenientes de la Conmebol.
wiki: Copa de Oro de la Concacaf 2003

title: El paso del Huracán Erika afectó a Tamaulipas y Nuevo León.
text: El huracán Erika fue un huracán débil que azotó el extremo noreste de México cerca de la frontera Con Estados Unidos a mediados de agosto de la temporada de huracanes del Atlántico de 2003. Erika fue el octavo ciclón tropical, la quinta tormenta tropical y el tercer huracán de la temporada.

title: Los Diablos Rojos del México se coronaron campeones de la Liga Mexicana de Béisbol.
text: La Temporada 2003 de la Liga Mexicana de Béisbol fue la edición número 79. Para esta temporada no hubo cambios de sede.

title: Se crea el grupo G20.
text: El G20 o Grupo de los 20 países en desarrollo, también conocido como G21,​ G22, G23 y G20+, es un grupo de 23 naciones en desarrollo establecido el 20 de agosto de 2003.

title: Se instala la LIX Legislatura del Congreso de la Unión de México.
text: La LIX Legislatura del Congreso de la Unión está conformada por los Senadores y los Diputados miembros de sus respectivas cámaras. Inició sus funciones el día 1 de septiembre de 2003 y concluyó el día 31 de agosto de 2006.
wiki: Anexo:LIX Legislatura del Congreso de la Unión de México

title: Se fundó Financiera Rural.
text: Financiera Nacional de Desarrollo Agropecuario, Rural, Forestal y Pesquero fue una institución de banca de desarrollo rural del Gobierno Federal sectorizado en la Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público (SHCP). Surgió en 2003 decretado por el presidente Vicente Fox Quesada con el objetivo de crear un sistema financiero rural eficiente que reemplazara al Banco Nacional de Crédito Rural (Banrural) el cual se encont…

title: Fahrenheit has its first issue published.
text: FAHRENHEITº is a bimonthly magazine of contemporary art and lifestyle that addresses themes from different disciplines of art, criticism and theory. It was founded in 2003 in Mexico City by Rubén José Marshall Tikalova.

title: The Chiapas Bridge is finished with being constructed.
text: The Chiapas Bridge is a steel bridge over a kilometer in length which spans the Nezahualcoyotl or Malpaso Dam in northern Chiapas, Mexico. Construction of the bridge began in 2002 and finished fourteen months later, voted the best infrastructure project in Mexico in 2004.

title: 2003 Colima earthquake.
text: An earthquake struck the Pacific Coast of Mexico on 21 January 2003 with a moment magnitude of 7.5. It had a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII.

title: The State of Mexico votes in a referendum on the death penalty. 82% of the 806,416 people who voted, voted Yes for the death penalty on crimes of murder, kidnapping, child theft and violent assaults.
text: Capital punishment has been abolished in Mexico since 15 March 2005. The last civilian execution in the country occurred in 1957, and the last military execution in 1961.

title: The National Commission for the Development of Indigenous Peoples goes into effect.
text: The National Institute of Indigenous Peoples is a decentralized agency of the Mexican Federal Public Administration. It was established on December 4, 2018, though the earliest Mexican government agency for indigenous matters was created in 1948.

title: 2003 Mexican legislative election
text: Legislative elections were held in Mexico on 6 July 2003. Although the National Action Party received the most votes, the Institutional Revolutionary Party won 224 of the 500 seats.

title: World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2003 in Cancun.
text: At the World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2003, trade ministers from 146 members of the World Trade Organization, representing 93 percent of global commerce, convened in Cancún, Mexico, in September 2003. The conference (the fifth WTO Ministerial Conference, or MC5) was held at the Cancún Centro de Convenciones, Cancún.
wiki: World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2003

title: Nuestra Belleza México 2003.
text: Nuestra Belleza México 2003, the 10th Nuestra Belleza México pageant, was held at the Teatro del Arte of Morelia, Michoacán, Mexico on September 5, 2003. Thirty-eight contestants of the Mexican Republic competed for the national title, which was won by Rosalva Luna from Sinaloa, who later competed in Miss Universe 2004 in Ecuador where she was a Semifinalist in the Top 15.

title: Optibús starts operations.
text: SIT Optibús is a bus rapid transit (BRT) system operating in León, Guanajuato, Mexico. Locally it is known also as "La Oruga" (the caterpillar), due to its use of articulated buses.

title: the Monterrey Arena is opened.
text: Arena Monterrey is an indoor arena in Monterrey, Nuevo León. It is primarily used for shows, concerts and indoor sports like indoor soccer, arena football and basketball.

title: 11: The United Nations Convention Against Corruption is opened for signing in Mérida, Yucatán.
text: The United Nations Convention Against Corruption is the only legally binding international anti-corruption multilateral treaty. Negotiated by member states of the United Nations (UN) it was adopted by the UN General Assembly in October 2003 and entered into force in December 2005.

title: Counter-terrorism base Ixtoc-Alfa is founded by the Mexican Navy.
text: Ixtoc-Alfa is a counter-terrorism base created by the Mexican Navy for the purpose of preventing terrorist attacks on the country's Gulf of Mexico oilfields. It was first opened on 22 December 2003.

title: Primera División de México Clausura 2003
text: Primera División de México Clausura 2003 is a Mexican football tournament - one of two short tournaments that take up the entire year to determine the champion(s) of Mexican football. It began on Saturday, January 11, 2003, and ran until May 17, when the regular season ended.

title: Primera División de México Apertura 2003
text: Primera División de México Apertura 2003 is a Mexican football tournament - one of two short tournaments that take up the entire year to determine the champion(s) of Mexican football. It began on Saturday 2 August 2003, and ran until 22 November, when the regular season ended.

title: Mexico win the 2003 CONCACAF Gold Cup
text: The 2003 CONCACAF Gold Cup was the seventh edition of the Gold Cup, the soccer championship of North America, Central America and the Caribbean. For the first time since 1993, the tournament was held in more than one country, with games played in both United States and Mexico.

title: 2003 Centrobasket held in Culiacán
text: This page shows the results of the Men's Central American and Caribbean Basketball Championship, also known as the 2003 Centrobasket, which was held in the city of Culiacán, Mexico from June 17 to June 22, 2003.

title: 2003 Mexican Figure Skating Championships
text: The Mexican Figure Skating Championships are an annual figure skating competition organized by the Mexican Federation of Figure Skating and Winter Sports (Spanish: Federación Mexicana de Patinaje Sobre Hielo y Deportes de Invierno) to crown the national champions of Mexico. Medals are awarded in men's singles, women's singles, and ice dance at the senior and junior levels, although each discipline may not necessar…

title: 2003 Gran Premio Telmex-Gigante
text: The 2003 Gran Premio Telmex-Gigante was the seventeenth round of the 2003 CART World Series season, held on October 12, 2003 at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City, Mexico.

title: 2003 MasterCard Truck Series season
text: The 2003 MasterCard Truck Series was the second and final season of MasterCard Truck Series. César Tiberio Jiménez was proclaimed champion.

title: 2003 Tecate Telmex Monterrey Grand Prix
text: The 2003 Tecate Telmex Monterrey Grand Prix was the second round of the 2003 CART World Series season, held on March 23, 2003 on the streets of Parque Fundidora in Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico.

title: Homenaje a Dos Leyendas: El Santo y Salvador Lutteroth (2003)
text: Homenaje a Dos Leyendas: El Santo y Salvador Lutteroth (Spanish for "Homage to Two Legends: El Santo and Salvador Lutteroth") was a professional wrestling supercard show event, scripted and produced by Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL; "World Wrestling Council"). The Dos Leyendas show took place on March 21, 2003 in CMLL's main venue, Arena México, Mexico City, Mexico.
wiki: Homenaje a Dos Leyendas: El Santo y Salvador Lutteroth (2003)

title: 2003 IIHF World U18 Championship Division III co-hosted with Bosnia
text: The 2003 IIHF World U18 Championship Division III was a pair of international under-18 ice hockey tournaments run by the International Ice Hockey Federation. The Division III tournaments made up the fourth level of competition at the 2003 IIHF World U18 Championships.
wiki: 2003 IIHF World U18 Championship Division III

title: 2003 Men's NORCECA Volleyball Championship Culiacan, Sinaloa
text: The 2003 Men's NORCECA Volleyball Championship was the 18th edition of the Men's Continental Volleyball Tournament, played by eight countries from September 25 to September 30, 2003, in Culiacan, Sinaloa.

title: 2003 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup Saltillo, Coahuila
text: The 2003 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup was the second edition of the annual women's volleyball tournament, played by eight countries from Monday June 30 to Saturday July 5, 2003 in Saltillo, Coahuila, Mexico. The intercontinental event served as a qualifier for the 2004 FIVB World Grand Prix.

title: 2003 Central American and Caribbean Cross Country Championships
text: The 2003 Central American and Caribbean Cross Country Championships took place on March 16, 2003. The races were held at the Club de Golf Acapulco in Acapulco, Mexico.
wiki: 2003 Central American and Caribbean Cross Country Championships

title: Mexico at the 2003 Pan American Games
text: Mexico participated at the 14th Pan American Games, held in Santo Domingo, the Dominican Republic, from 1 to 17 August 2003.
wiki: Mexico at the 2003 Pan American Games

title: 2003 Pan American Race Walking Cup from San Diego, California, United States to Tijuana, Baja California.
text: The 2003 Pan American Race Walking Cup was held in two locations: both 20 kilometres events in Chula Vista, California, United States, on 15 March. The track of the Cup ran in the Marina Parkway at Chula Vista Marina.
